skill.description: Coordinate parallel design and implementation workflows using omakase-off, cookoff, and judge phases for comparing software approaches.
skill.summary: Guide AI agents through parallel design exploration, implementation competitions, and structured judging.

security_audit.summary: Static findings mostly matched Markdown backticks, code fences, and ordinary prose rather than executable code. No evidence found of credential access, network exfiltration, or prompt-injection text. One medium workflow risk remains because cleanup instructions can remove worktrees and force-delete branches.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running git worktree remove or git branch -D, and document how to preserve unmerged work.

static_findings.snippet: - `cookoff` - Same design, multiple cooks compete (each creates own plan + implements)
| `writing-plans` | `superpowers:writing-plans` | Each agent writes their own implementation plan |
| `executing-plans` | `superpowers:executing-plans` | Execute plan tasks sequentially with verificat
| `parallel-agents` | `superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents` | Dispatch multiple Task tools in si
| `verification` | `superpowers:verification-before-completion` | Run command, read output, THEN cla
| `fresh-eyes` | `fresh-eyes-review:skills` (2389) | 2-5 min review for security, logic, edge cases
| `judge` | `test-kitchen:judge` | Scoring framework with checklists (MUST invoke at Phase 4) |
Use `parallel-agents` pattern. Send ONE message with multiple Task tool calls:
| `writing-plans` | 3 | Each subagent creates their own implementation plan |
| `parallel-agents` | 3 | Dispatch ALL subagents in SINGLE message |
| `verification` | 3, 5 | Before claiming done; before declaring winner |
| `judge` | 4 | **INVOKE** for scoring framework (loads fresh, ensures format compliance) |
Reason: Clean fresh-eyes review, solid data-layer-first architecture
2. Best guess - I'll pick what seems best and proceed with one plan
- `cookoff` - Same recipe, multiple cooks compete (same plan, multiple implementations)
| `brainstorming` | Modified flow with passive slot detection |
| `parallel-agents` | Dispatch all variant subagents in parallel |
| `scenario-testing` | Run same scenarios against all variants |
| `fresh-eyes` | Quality review on survivors → input for judge |

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Git Cleanup Requires Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow instructs agents to remove worktrees and force-delete branches after selecting a winner. These commands can delete unmerged local work if executed without explicit confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both referenced sections contain cleanup steps for git worktree removal and branch deletion. The commands are legitimate workflow cleanup, but force deletion can lose local work.

content.value_statement: Complex software choices can be hard to judge from discussion alone. Test Kitchen guides parallel designs, implementations, reviews, and winner selection.
actual_capabilities: Routes build and implementation requests to omakase-off or cookoff workflows.
Offers brainstorm or omakase modes before detailed design work begins.
Detects architectural indecision and proposes parallel implementation variants.
Runs cookoff workflows where multiple agents create independent plans from one design.
Uses a judge worksheet with five scoring criteria and hard gates.
Documents plans, results, winner selection, and cleanup steps.
limitations: Full automation requires compatible subagent tooling and optional helper skills.
It may create worktrees, branches, plan files, and result files in a repository.
It needs clear requirements or scenarios to compare variants fairly.
Cleanup commands can remove worktrees or branches and need confirmation.

use_cases.title: Compare implementation strategies
use_cases.description: Run several agents against one approved design, then score their results with a shared rubric.

use_cases.title: Explore architectural options
use_cases.description: Turn uncertainty about storage, authentication, or framework choices into working variants for evaluation.

use_cases.title: Select a prototype winner
use_cases.description: Review tests, scenario results, fresh-eyes feedback, and judge scores before choosing one variant.

prompt_templates.title: Start a guided build
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner entry point for a new feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use test-kitchen to help me build <feature>. Start by asking whether I want brainstorming or omakase mode.

prompt_templates.title: Explore two approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Run omakase-off for <project>. Explore <decision A> versus <decision B>, then compare variants with tests.

prompt_templates.title: Run a cookoff
prompt_templates.scenario: Implement an approved design with multiple agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use cookoff for this approved design. Spawn <N> parallel implementations, require separate plans, and judge the results.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate full evaluation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with planning, testing, judging, and cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate a full test-kitchen workflow for <feature>: detect architectural slots, create variants, run scenario testing, use fresh-eyes review, invoke judge, and prepare a result summary.

output_examples.input: I need to build a CLI todo app, and I am unsure about storage.
output_examples.output: The assistant offers brainstorming or omakase mode, identifies JSON versus SQLite as a slot, and compares variants through tests.

output_examples.input: The design is approved. Implement it.
output_examples.output: The assistant presents single-agent, cookoff, or local coding options, then runs independent plans for the chosen path.

output_examples.input: Three variants passed tests. Choose a winner.
output_examples.output: The assistant applies the judge checklist, reports scores, names a winner, and lists trade-offs.

best_practices: Confirm the workflow mode and number of variants before spawning agents.
Keep each variant tied to the same requirements and verification criteria.
Review cleanup commands before removing worktrees or branches.
anti_patterns: Using cookoff without a shared design or approved requirements.
Letting variants skip tests, scenario checks, or review steps.
Deleting branches or worktrees before the user accepts a winner.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It coordinates parallel design and implementation workflows, then helps compare the results with structured judging.

faq.question: When should I use omakase-off?
faq.answer: Use it when the best architecture is unclear and multiple approaches should be tested in parallel.

faq.question: When should I use cookoff?
faq.answer: Use it after a design is approved and you want multiple independent implementations of that design.

faq.question: Does it write code directly?
faq.answer: It can route to agents or local implementation, but its main role is workflow orchestration and evaluation.

faq.question: Does it require Git worktrees?
faq.answer: It recommends worktrees for isolation, but teams can adapt the workflow if worktrees are unavailable.

faq.question: Is it safe on an active repository?
faq.answer: Use it carefully. Confirm branch, worktree, and cleanup actions before allowing commands that modify the repository.
